methodLimitations: SVG-based em-height simulations: opening files at 100% browser zoom approximates CSS pixels but physical size differs by device display, screen scaling, and print settings.
The new glyphs do not yet have final root assignments, so strings are ID-based pseudo-text and not valid translated Cuspell spells.
Spacing used is an illustrative uniform 0.6em glyph advance with additional margin, not final font bearings/kerning/hinting or a real installed font.
Punctuation draft shapes are not yet all approved; source-derived period, colon, and question marks are previously user selected.
Full 234-source atlas uses SVG symbol reuse with original paths; local PNGs are based on raster crops of previously source-rendered comparisons and represent only 62 distinct designs.
Do not remove any glyph without direct user choice; no source artwork changed.
recommendedNextStep: User review mixed-size sheets and indicate unacceptable small-size collisions; then approve remaining punctuation drafts or request adjustments; determine legibility floor before mapping 218 glyphs and creating font.

userReadabilityDecision.instruction: Under 18-20 yes, But we will be working with 20 and up(think 32/34) so it's fine.

workflowAfterReadability: Finish visual approval of all 13 player-facing punctuation and grammar SVGs; revise only upon explicit user feedback.

Before any root-to-shape assignment, build PC-installable test TTF/OTF with ALL 234 surviving normalized shapes as separate glyphs, plus punctuation. Use temporary nonsemantic Private Use Area Unicode mapping and companion searchable glyph ID map/typing tester.
User installs test font locally and tests at >=20px, especially 32px/34px, reporting actual display/spacing/typing problems. Fix prototype font and test again.
ONLY AFTER successful on-PC trial, assign 218 semantic/numeric signs to selected glyphs and reserve surplus 16; later build finalized language font.
